extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and peer reviewers invited to review manuscripts for Cell Press journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and expectations for scientists performing peer review for Cell Press journals, covering ethical, procedural, and editorial-quality criteria for evaluating manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest and Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should be sensitive to potential conflicts of interest, both real and perceived. It is not appropriate to discuss unpublished manuscripts at laboratory meetings or journal clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid real or perceived conflicts; maintain strict confidentiality of unpublished manuscripts and do not share or discuss them in lab meetings, journal clubs, or other settings where confidentiality would be compromised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration and Co-Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can collaborate with trainees (graduate students and post-docs) in manuscript evaluation, though reviewers should keep the number of collaborators to a minimum and include the identities of all individuals involved in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted to involve trainees but minimize the number of collaborators and disclose the names/identities of all persons who contributed to the review (co-reviewers/trainees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell Press journals consider ten days to be sufficient time to review a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to complete reviews promptly; the journal expects ~10 days to be a sufficient review period and reviewers should adhere to agreed timelines or communicate delays to editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not upload their peer review report into AI tools, and generative AI or AI-assisted technologies should not be used by reviewers to assist in the scientific review of a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use generative AI or AI-assisted technologies to perform or assist the scientific evaluation; do not paste confidential review content (reports) into external AI tools or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: For editorial consistency and fairness to authors, reviewers who agree to review one version of a manuscript should commit to reviewing future revisions if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you accept to review a manuscript, be prepared to review subsequent revised versions to ensure consistent editorial assessment and fairness to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit for the Journal's Scope and Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The fit of the study for the journal's scope and interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the manuscript aligns with the journal's topical scope, readership, and editorial priorities as part of the overall editorial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance in the Context of the Field
rubrics_metrics.description: The advance in the context of the field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the novelty and significance of the work: does the study provide a clear advance relative to existing knowledge in the field?

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for the Conclusions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the data, analysis, and methods adequately support the authors' conclusions, including rigor of experiments, appropriateness of analyses, and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Journal Submission / Portfolio Fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell Press operates a multi-journal submission system where reviewers may evaluate manuscripts that could fit multiple journals in the portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that manuscripts may be assessed for fit across multiple journals in the Cell Press portfolio; reviewers may be asked to evaluate suitability for different journal outlets and should comment on relative fit when appropriate.
